title: Creator Broadcast Message Delivery
purpose: Show the flow of creator broadcast (mass message) delivery to all active subscribers, highlighting the N+1 query pattern and fire-and-forget nature
audience: Backend developers, creator experience engineers, performance engineers
description: A creator sends a mass message to all active subscribers via POST /api/v1/messages/mass-message. The message service fetches all active subscriptions for the creator, then iterates each subscriber to check notification preferences, call sendDirectMessage (inserts into messages table), and broadcast via Socket.IO to the subscriber's room. The flow exhibits an N+1 query pattern where one query fetches subscribers then N individual sendDirectMessage calls are made sequentially. There is no retry on individual message failure and no rate limiting on broadcast frequency.

validationRules: Creator must have protectAndCreator middleware (JWT + creator role)
Message body must be non-empty string
Subject and body required in request payload
Creator must have completed onboarding (creator_data must exist)
minTierId optional — if provided, must be a valid tier ID from creator's tiers
businessRules: N+1 query pattern: one query fetches all subscribers, then N individual sendDirectMessage calls
No batch insert — each subscriber gets individual INSERT + Socket.IO broadcast
No retry on individual message failure — fire-and-forget semantics
No rate limiting on broadcast — creator can send unlimited broadcasts
{{username}} template variable replaced with subscriber's display name per message
minTierId filter allows tier-gated broadcast (only subscribers at or above specified tier)
securityConsiderations: Broadcast restricted to creator role — protectAndCreator middleware
Creator can send unlimited messages — no rate limiting (spam risk)
Subscriber opt-out respected via preferences.notifications.massMessages flag
No message content moderation on broadcast
Message data includes personal subscriber information (display name in template)
performanceConsiderations: N+1 query pattern: 1 subscription query + N message insert + N Socket.IO broadcasts — scales linearly with subscriber count
Synchronous iteration — each subscriber processed sequentially before next starts
For creators with thousands of subscribers, this endpoint could time out (no background job queue)
No batching — each subscriber causes individual DB write and Socket.IO event
Memory usage grows with subscriber list size (all records loaded in memory)

annotations.label: 🔴 N+1 Query Pattern
annotations.description: One query fetches subscribers, then N individual sendDirectMessage calls with individual DB writes and Socket.IO broadcasts.

annotations.label: 🟡 Fire-and-forget — No Retry
annotations.description: Individual message failures are logged but not retried. No delivery guarantee beyond best-effort.

annotations.label: 🟡 No Rate Limiting
annotations.description: Creator can send unlimited broadcasts in any time period. No throttle or cooldown.

annotations.label: 🟡 No Background Queue
annotations.description: All processing happens synchronously in the request-response cycle. For large subscriber bases, this blocks the HTTP response.
